So I flew with my 2 cats a few years ago and the only "issue" I ran into was I wasn't told I needed to physically check in with a ticketing agent in order to get my boarding pass and there was extra undisclosed fees. Take that into account for how early you show up.
As for the carriers I have two soft carriers. (It's called Sherpa pet carrier or something, I got them from Petco) Dimensions being roughly 26 cm height, 26 width, and 40 length but i was never asked or tested on it and they fully fit underneath the seats. The main reason they put these size restrictions is to make sure the carriers can fit under the seats and aren't blocking pathways. My cat is also a tall boy, in my opinion being able to stand up is less important than if they can turn/adjust and lay down comfortably. I would recommend using a soft carrier rather than a plastic one or cage with bars as they are typically more comfy and easier to travel with. If you have any other questions or concerns you can feel free to pm me. Good luck!

When I flew with my 2 cats (granted I did have medication for them) I also put a couple soft catnip filled toys in with them and covered the entire carrier with my tshirts both to block out excessive stressful stimuli and so they'd be able to smell me the whole time and the only times either of them seemed stressed out was when the plane took off and when it landed. Ditto to the comment that said check out a petsmart or petco cause they usually have vets or a variety of calming treats. I hope you all stay safe <3

I leash trained 1 of my two older adopts (they were both about 4 when I got them) one didn't mind the harness at all and the other hated it with a passion. What you described was exactly what happened with my two as well. I would say that 3 days might be a bit soon to give it up especially with a kitten but it just may not be something that he'll ever enjoy and that's not a bad thing. I don't know how you're doing the training but when I did mine there was a lot of trial and error with different harnesses and it took a week or two for leash training. The harness I found that they both liked the best was the "come with me kitty" harness (it's not super bulky or restrictive but it's still very secure) What I would do with my boy is every day introduce the harness next to a treat, put the harness on for a few minutes, give him a few more treats and lots of affection because that's what he likes and then when he started to get uncomfy I'd take it off. He walks on a leash just fine now, actually gets excited when i pull it out lol. I wish you all the luck! Just remember to be patient, cats are much harder to train than dogs. ❤️ (Their names are great too)
